newsitem.title: USA: Cool weather may slow Midwest spring planting.
newsitem.headline: Cool weather may slow Midwest spring planting.

text.p: Cool weather forecast through the weekend should keep Midwest soil temperatures lower than preferred for corn and soybean planting, meteorologists said.
"Planting is being held up by cool soil temperatures, but if they want to they can," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
Farmers were eager to plant corn and soybeans this week. Grain dealers said some sowing was under way, with farmers hoping soils will soon warm enough to allow the seeds to germinate.
Forecasts called for mostly dry weather in the Midwest until Sunday. Remembering rain delays in 1996, many farmers this year will plant despite cool soils.
The Midwest should turn warmer by mid-week next week followed by another cold front the weekend of May 3, the meteorologists said.
Scattered showers were forecast Sunday and Monday across Missouri, southern and eastern Illinois and in the eastern Midwest, with amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches likely.
"That's about the only area of the Corn Belt that we see any significant moisture," said Craig Solberg, Freese-Notis Weather meteorologist.
